name: German Chamomile
imageAlt: Illustration of chamomile flowers with white petals and yellow centers
description: A cheerful annual covered in small daisy-like flowers with a sweet, apple-like scent. The dried flower heads are the world's best-known herbal tea, and the plant readily self-seeds in the garden.

growingConditions.watering: Regular, light watering; do not let seedlings dry out
growingConditions.hardinessZone: Annual in all zones (Roman chamomile is hardy in zones 4-9)

uses: Dried flower heads brewed as a calming tea
Gentle skin rinses and herbal baths
Edible garnish for salads and cakes
Chamomile tea is a classic evening drink to help you relax and wind down before sleep
Traditionally used to settle an upset stomach, gas and cramps
Cooled tea used as a mouth rinse or a soothing wash for minor skin irritation
benefits: Contains apigenin, an antioxidant linked to its mild calming effect
May ease mild digestive discomfort when taken as tea
medicinal.caution: People allergic to ragweed, daisies, marigolds or chrysanthemums may react to chamomile. Ask your doctor first if you take blood thinners or are pregnant.

video.title: How To Grow, Harvest & Make Chamomile Tea

taste: Gentle, sweet and floral, with a honey and apple-like flavor.
sideEffects: Can cause allergic reactions in people allergic to ragweed, daisies, marigolds or chrysanthemums
Very strong tea can sometimes cause nausea

safety.allergy: Chamomile belongs to the daisy family. People allergic to ragweed, daisies, marigolds or chrysanthemums may get hay fever symptoms, a rash or, rarely, a serious reaction. Stop using it and see a doctor if you feel unwell.
safety.pregnancy: Ask your doctor before using chamomile regularly during pregnancy.
safety.pets: Chamomile can be toxic to cats and dogs and may cause an upset stomach or skin irritation, so keep them away from the plant.
safety.medications: Chamomile may add to sleepy effects of sedatives and may affect blood thinners such as warfarin. Ask your doctor if you take them.

temperature: A cool-season herb. Seeds sprout at about 15-21 °C, plants grow best at about 15-25 °C, and German chamomile can tolerate a light frost.
harvest: Pick the flower heads when the petals are flat or just starting to droop, in dry mid-morning. Harvest every few days, because picking encourages more flowers.
storage: Spread the flowers on a screen in a shady, airy place until crisp, which takes one to two weeks. Store in an airtight jar away from light for up to a year.
dailyLife: Brew dried flowers as an evening tea
Add a few fresh flowers to salads or desserts
Use a cooled tea as a gentle skin rinse
tips: Sow seeds on the surface, because they need light to sprout
Let a few flowers go to seed so it self-sows next year
It does well in poor soil, too much feeding gives fewer flowers

origin.details: German chamomile is native to central and eastern Europe and western Asia. It has been brewed as a calming drink since ancient Egypt, Greece and Rome.
